Title: Your BA baseline
Practice task: Score yourself 1–5 in discovery, requirements, process, data, testing and communication; record a 90-second introduction.
Acceptance check: Six scores with one real example each; keep the recording for Day 90.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Choose the right problem
Practice task: Frame a simulated dock-booking exception problem: who is affected, current pain, business impact and desired outcome.
Acceptance check: One-page brief; separate known facts, assumptions and unmeasured baselines.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Draw the boundary
Practice task: Map suppliers, planners, warehouse, carrier and proposed exception service; write five scope exclusions.
Acceptance check: At least five external actors, labelled data flows and an agreed problem boundary.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Map the stakeholders
Practice task: Create an eight-person stakeholder register and RACI for approval, booking, escalation and reporting.
Acceptance check: One accountable role per activity; communication preferences and decision rights captured.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Find the cause
Practice task: Explore late delivery changes and define three testable root-cause hypotheses.
Acceptance check: Distinguish symptom from cause; give evidence needed to test each hypothesis.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Define value
Practice task: Define on-time delivery, exception resolution time and slot utilisation with grain, numerator and denominator.
Acceptance check: Three KPI definitions including owner, source, exclusions and baseline collection plan.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Dungeon 01: the problem brief
Practice task: Combine Days 1–6 into a concise discovery brief and deliver a three-minute stakeholder playback.
Acceptance check: Scope, stakeholders, hypotheses and value measures are consistent; note three improvements.
Speaking drill: Explain the business problem in 60 seconds: headline, who is affected, evidence needed, decision.

Title: Prepare your interviews
Practice task: Write ten open questions for a warehouse planner; add consent, timing and evidence prompts.
Acceptance check: Questions avoid leading the witness and cover exceptions, workarounds and business rules.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Simulate an interview
Practice task: Role-play planner and analyst; capture five needs and label all responses as simulated.
Acceptance check: Separate quotes, interpretation and assumptions; confirm the five needs in a summary.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Plan a workshop
Practice task: Design a 45-minute discovery workshop with purpose, roles, activities and decisions.
Acceptance check: Every agenda section has timing and an output; include a conflict and parking-lot plan.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Map today’s flow
Practice task: Map the as-is dock exception flow with start/end events, decision gateways and handoffs.
Acceptance check: Four lanes, two exception routes, owners and input/output definitions; no orphan steps.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Capture hidden rules
Practice task: Write rules for available capacity, carrier lateness, approval and escalation.
Acceptance check: Decision table covers normal, boundary and invalid cases; flag assumptions for validation.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Design tomorrow’s flow
Practice task: Create a to-be flow with human approval before booking changes and compare it with the as-is.
Acceptance check: Each gap has an owner, proposed change and intended benefit; preserve an exception route.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Dungeon 02: discovery playback
Practice task: Present as-is, to-be and unresolved questions in five slides; record a four-minute playback.
Acceptance check: Ask for three explicit decisions and capture owner/date for each unresolved issue.
Speaking drill: Give a 90-second playback: what you heard, what is uncertain, and what you need confirmed.

Title: Separate requirements
Technique: Business, stakeholder, solution and transition requirements
Practice task: Draft twelve requirements for the dock exception solution and classify each.
Acceptance check: Each requirement has a unique ID, source, rationale and category.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Make them measurable
Practice task: Rewrite six vague requirements into atomic testable statements.
Acceptance check: Each rewritten requirement has observable success conditions and avoids undefined terms such as fast.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Write the BRD
Practice task: Build a lean BRD covering goals, scope, actors, assumptions, requirements and constraints.
Acceptance check: Every requirement traces back to a business objective; include a version and approval log.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Model the user journey
Technique: Use cases, alternate and exception flows
Practice task: Write a Reschedule Delivery use case with preconditions, trigger, normal flow and failure routes.
Acceptance check: Include no-capacity, approval-rejected and duplicate-request scenarios.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Specify quality attributes
Practice task: Define response-time, availability, access, audit and usability requirements for the prototype.
Acceptance check: Five measurable requirements with a verification method; targets are assumptions, not production promises.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Prioritise fairly
Practice task: Prioritise twelve requirements using business value, risk, effort and dependency notes.
Acceptance check: Explain three tradeoffs and why each must-have is needed for the minimum viable outcome.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Dungeon 03: requirements review
Practice task: Create an RTM linking objectives → requirements → acceptance tests and resolve two conflicts.
Acceptance check: No orphan requirement; all high-priority needs have an owner and test reference.
Speaking drill: Explain one requirement in plain language, then give its acceptance example and business value.

Title: Learn delivery models
Practice task: Compare a fixed compliance change with evolving booking automation; choose an approach for each.
Acceptance check: Explain uncertainty, governance and feedback needs; identify Scrum accountabilities correctly.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Build the backlog
Practice task: Create three epics and twelve user stories for the exception solution.
Acceptance check: Each story has user, need and value; split stories that contain multiple independent outcomes.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Define acceptance
Practice task: Write three acceptance scenarios each for booking approval, duplicate handling and capacity checking.
Acceptance check: Positive, negative and boundary scenarios are unambiguous and observable.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Slice the work
Practice task: Map the user journey and choose one thin end-to-end release.
Acceptance check: MVP includes submission, validation, approval and feedback; defer low-value scope explicitly.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Plan a sprint
Practice task: Refine six stories and create a mock sprint with a Sprint Goal and capacity assumptions.
Acceptance check: No committed story exceeds assumed capacity; Definition of Done includes testing and evidence.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Handle a change request
Practice task: Assess a new auto-approve request against privacy, risk, scope, cost and acceptance tests.
Acceptance check: Give options, recommendation and approval owner; update RTM and backlog versions.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Dungeon 04: sprint simulation
Practice task: Walk through the board, demo two paper-prototype stories and run a start/stop/continue retrospective.
Acceptance check: Explain a blocked story and a tradeoff; log one measurable improvement for the next sprint.
Speaking drill: Give a 60-second update: goal, progress, blocker, next step and one clear request.

Title: Sketch the experience
Practice task: Draw an exception inbox, request detail and approval screen; annotate empty/error states.
Acceptance check: A planner can identify status, owner and next action; capture three usability observations.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Boss 01: discovery to delivery
Practice task: Assemble your discovery + requirements portfolio; record a five-minute sponsor briefing.
Acceptance check: Include problem, BPMN, BRD, RTM, backlog and prototype; finish with a recommendation and decision request.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Inspect the data
Practice task: Open the provided synthetic shipments CSV; document row grain, columns, nulls and data types.
Acceptance check: State that it is training data; identify duplicates before calculating KPIs.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Clean reproducibly
Practice task: Import shipments into Power Query and define repeatable cleaning steps.
Acceptance check: Keep raw input intact; justify duplicate and missing-date rules in a transformation log.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Build useful formulas
Practice task: Map carrier names and calculate delivered, late and exception counts by carrier.
Acceptance check: Reconcile formulas to a small manual sample; define treatment of open shipments.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Summarise operations
Practice task: Build carrier and warehouse pivots; use a Pareto view to prioritise exception reasons.
Acceptance check: Counts reconcile to cleaned rows; conclusions include sample size and limitations.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Dungeon 05: spreadsheet control
Practice task: Create a one-page operations tracker with inputs, calculations, checks and a user note.
Acceptance check: Three reconciliation checks pass and invalid inputs are visibly flagged.
Speaking drill: Explain one metric: definition, denominator, data limitation and operational implication.

Title: Define the data model
Practice task: Model Shipment, Carrier, Warehouse and Exception with primary and foreign keys.
Acceptance check: Declare grain and one-to-many relationships; avoid repeating carrier names on dimension rows.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Query your first table
Practice task: Load the starter SQL in SQLite or adapt it to SQL Server; write six filter queries.
Acceptance check: Predict row counts for two queries and confirm NULL uses IS NULL rather than equality.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Aggregate with care
Technique: GROUP BY, HAVING, COUNT, SUM, AVG
Practice task: Calculate delivered counts, average transit time and late rate by carrier.
Acceptance check: Exclude undelivered rows from delivery KPI denominators; show numerator and denominator.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Join without inflation
Technique: INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, join cardinality
Practice task: Join shipments to carriers and warehouses and compare row counts before/after.
Acceptance check: No unexplained increase in shipment rows; unmatched keys are reported separately.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Express business logic
Practice task: Classify shipments as open, on-time or late and flag invalid delivery dates.
Acceptance check: Five edge cases have expected outputs; use dialect-appropriate date functions.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Break a complex question down
Practice task: Find carriers with a worse late rate than the network average using a CTE.
Acceptance check: Explain grain at each step and verify the result on one carrier manually.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Dungeon 06: SQL investigation
Practice task: Rank carriers and identify duplicate external references using ROW_NUMBER; save eight reviewed queries.
Acceptance check: Add comments with business question, denominator and limitation for every KPI query.
Speaking drill: Walk through your query in plain language before discussing SQL syntax.

Title: Connect and transform
Tools: Power BI Desktop or Excel fallback
Practice task: Load the synthetic data and carrier dimension into Power BI; apply documented cleaning rules.
Acceptance check: Refresh succeeds; row counts match your Excel control totals.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Model for analysis
Practice task: Create fact shipments, carrier, warehouse and date dimensions with explicit relationship directions.
Acceptance check: Keys are unique on dimension sides; distinguish dispatch date from delivery date.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Write measures
Practice task: Create Delivered, Late Deliveries, Late Rate and Open Shipments measures.
Acceptance check: DIVIDE handles a zero denominator; totals match your SQL on the same cleaned data.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Design for a decision
Practice task: Build an overview with filters, trend, carrier comparison and exception detail.
Acceptance check: Every visual answers a named stakeholder question; labels and colour do not mislead.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Analyse causes carefully
Practice task: Compare late rates across carrier, warehouse and service level.
Acceptance check: Show denominators; distinguish an observed association from a verified cause.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Add drill-through
Practice task: Add a carrier detail page and test filter interactions with three user tasks.
Acceptance check: Users can answer the three tasks without changing the data; document reset instructions.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Dungeon 07: insight briefing
Practice task: Record a three-minute report walkthrough: finding, evidence, limitation, action.
Acceptance check: Reconcile the report to SQL and Excel; make one recommendation without inventing business savings.
Speaking drill: Present one finding with evidence, limitation and a recommendation in two minutes.

Title: Trace the system landscape
Technique: System context, SAP TM/MM and TMS mapping
Practice task: Draw a conceptual ERP → TMS → WMS landscape using only generic training examples.
Acceptance check: Label master vs transactional data and system of record; do not imply access to live SAP or Blue Yonder.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Understand a contract
Practice task: Inspect a public practice request in Postman and write a mock delivery-change JSON contract.
Acceptance check: Specify required fields, types, example values and expected success response.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Design failure behaviour
Practice task: Document duplicate, invalid capacity, unauthorised and unavailable-service outcomes.
Acceptance check: Each failure has user feedback, retry guidance, logging and an owner.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Map source to target
Practice task: Map carrier code, delivery date, slot and warehouse across two mock systems.
Acceptance check: Include source/target types, required flags, transformation and rejected-record handling.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Define governance
Practice task: Create a carrier master ownership matrix and change/approval flow.
Acceptance check: Every critical field has an owner, validation rule and audit requirement.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Protect integration quality
Practice task: Design an integration checklist for missed events, duplicates and partial failures.
Acceptance check: Specify how counts/totals reconcile and how a human can resolve failed messages.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Dungeon 08: integration review
Practice task: Present a delivery change journey across mailbox, exception service, approver and TMS.
Acceptance check: Show happy path plus timeout and rejection; align payloads with the source-to-target mapping.
Speaking drill: Explain the system flow to a warehouse planner without using unexplained technical terms.

Title: Plan the test strategy
Practice task: Define UAT scope, roles, environment, entry/exit criteria and test data needs.
Acceptance check: Prioritise risks; distinguish system integration testing from business acceptance.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Write executable cases
Practice task: Write ten UAT cases linked to requirements with steps, inputs and expected results.
Acceptance check: Cover full slot, last available slot, invalid date, duplicate and rejected approval.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Prepare safe test data
Technique: Test data design, anonymisation, negative cases
Practice task: Create normal, boundary, invalid and missing-data test records.
Acceptance check: Use synthetic records only; include expected results and isolate destructive scenarios.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Boss 02: the evidence gate
Practice task: Demo the dashboard and integration contract; show the UAT plan and KPI reconciliation.
Acceptance check: Supply cleaned data, SQL, dashboard screenshots, mapping and ten UAT cases; log all unresolved defects.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Run and triage
Technique: Test execution, severity vs priority, defect lifecycle
Practice task: Execute the ten UAT cases against your paper prototype or mock rules and log results.
Acceptance check: Record actual vs expected, evidence and severity; label simulation clearly.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Recommend readiness
Practice task: Calculate requirement-to-test coverage; create a release recommendation with residual risks.
Acceptance check: Explain blocked vs failed vs passed tests; do not treat high coverage as proof of quality.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Dungeon 09: UAT command
Practice task: Host a mock UAT triage and write an evidence-based conditional go/no-go decision.
Acceptance check: Include defect owners, business impact and sign-off criteria; no fabricated stakeholder approvals.
Speaking drill: Defend a test outcome: business risk, evidence, recommendation and decision owner.

Title: Plan the change
Practice task: Map what changes for planners, carriers, warehouse operators and support.
Acceptance check: For each group, document impact, readiness risk, training and support owner.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Write an operational SOP
Practice task: Write a delivery-change SOP with trigger, roles, steps, escalation and version control.
Acceptance check: Someone unfamiliar with the design can follow the steps and find the escalation route.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Make training useful
Practice task: Create a five-slide planner training pack and deliver a short demonstration.
Acceptance check: Include one normal task and one recovery task; add three teach-back questions.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Select the automation
Practice task: Design mailbox classification → capacity check → human approval → update → audit.
Acceptance check: List permissions, error queue and manual fallback; keep live external actions disabled in practice.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Build a safe prototype
Practice task: Build a mock flow using manual/sample input and route the decision to a test log.
Acceptance check: Normal, rejection and malformed-input cases produce expected mock outcomes; no live booking updates.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Measure improvement
Practice task: Design a two-week pilot measurement plan for resolution time and manual touchpoints.
Acceptance check: Define comparison group/time window, sample size caveat, guardrails and data owner.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Dungeon 10: adoption launch
Practice task: Package SOP, training, pilot plan and a rollback decision tree.
Acceptance check: Name launch owner, rollback triggers and support routes; separate expected from proven benefits.
Speaking drill: Teach the changed process with one normal example and one exception.

Title: Choose your capstone
Practice task: Pick one end-to-end supply-chain BA case and write a one-page charter.
Acceptance check: One clear decision, three measurable outcomes and a small enough scope to finish in two weeks.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Rebuild discovery independently
Practice task: Create a new stakeholder register and as-is process for the capstone without copying blindly.
Acceptance check: Label assumptions and evidence gaps; include three questions that could change your design.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Design the solution options
Practice task: Compare manual improvement, light automation and system enhancement.
Acceptance check: Use explicit scoring weights, indicative costs and uncertainty; justify a recommendation.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Specify the capstone
Practice task: Create ten requirements, six stories and acceptance criteria for the selected option.
Acceptance check: Each story traces to a need and test; version the scope and decision log.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Create the data evidence
Technique: Data preparation, quality checks, analytical SQL
Practice task: Use the synthetic shipment data or your own safe sample to answer three capstone questions.
Acceptance check: Save reproducible queries and validation checks with dataset limitations.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Build the decision view
Practice task: Create a report or wireframe that supports the capstone decision.
Acceptance check: Demonstrate three user questions and state what cannot be concluded from the sample.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Dungeon 11: architecture review
Technique: Design review, risk assessment, peer critique
Practice task: Review your charter, requirements, process, data and prototype as a coherent solution.
Acceptance check: Resolve three inconsistencies and record why you accepted remaining risks.
Speaking drill: Pitch your chosen option: problem, evidence, alternatives, risk and explicit ask.

Title: Test your capstone
Practice task: Execute eight capstone acceptance scenarios against the mock solution.
Acceptance check: Store inputs, expected/actual results and evidence; trace every critical requirement.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Prepare the recommendation
Practice task: Build five slides: problem, evidence, options, recommendation and next steps.
Acceptance check: State one decision request with owner and date; include risks and uncertain assumptions.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Translate your experience
Practice task: Draft three truthful BA interview stories from your operations and project experience.
Acceptance check: Distinguish your action from team action; use only figures you can explain and defend.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Lead a difficult conversation
Practice task: Role-play a sponsor demanding auto-approval despite operational risk.
Acceptance check: Acknowledge their goal, ask two probes, explain tradeoff and offer a controlled alternative.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Run a case interview
Practice task: Spend 30 minutes on a late-delivery case: clarify, structure, analyse and recommend.
Acceptance check: State assumptions aloud; calculate one KPI correctly and explain a limitation.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Speak with impact
Practice task: Record your capstone briefing twice; emphasise the headline and explicit ask.
Acceptance check: Compare clarity, audible volume, pace and conclusion with Day 1; choose three improvements.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Dungeon 12: mock panel
Practice task: Deliver a six-minute capstone demo and answer five challenging questions.
Acceptance check: No unsupported impact claims; each answer gives a position, evidence and next action.
Speaking drill: Answer a challenge with a position, evidence and practical next step; record and review it.

Title: Package the portfolio
Practice task: Create a readme for each of three case packs with problem, role, artifacts and limits.
Acceptance check: Remove confidential data and label all simulated projects; links open correctly.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.

Title: Audit the weak spots
Practice task: Repeat Day 1’s six-skill self-assessment using artifacts as evidence.
Acceptance check: Identify the two weakest skills and perform one focused correction for each.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.

Title: Tailor your profile
Technique: Role mapping, CV evidence, skill matrix
Practice task: Map your portfolio to three target BA role descriptions and refine four truthful CV bullets.
Acceptance check: Every bullet supports a relevant requirement and avoids invented metrics or experience.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.

Title: Rehearse the final raid
Practice task: Rehearse a ten-minute end-to-end walkthrough and prepare five likely objections.
Acceptance check: Explain business need, process, requirements, data, tests and adoption in one connected story.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.

Title: Prepare the next cycle
Practice task: Review completed artifacts and set a realistic 30-day continuation plan.
Acceptance check: Choose three priorities with observable success criteria; plan rest and maintenance.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.

Title: Boss 03: BA ascension
Practice task: Ship three portfolio packs and record your final ten-minute BA case defence.
Acceptance check: Compare to Day 1; verify traceability, calculations, test evidence and communication; document gaps honestly.
Speaking drill: Deliver a confident headline first; pause, support it with evidence and finish with an ask.
